newsitem.title: POLAND: Polish shares set record, seen off highs.
newsitem.headline: Polish shares set record, seen off highs.

text.p: Gains by some heavyweights pushed the Warsaw bourse WIG index to a 33-month high despite falls by most stocks and analysts expected a profit-taking correction after the market's surge of over 20 percent since mid-December.

The main market's WIG index rose 34.4 points, or 0.2 percent, to 15,979.3, and turnover held virtually flat at 175.6 million zlotys ($60.6 million) on both markets as 50 issues fell, 20 rose and 16 were flat.
"I believe we will have a correction...a kind of cooling down, which would be good for the market, which has risen so rapidly," said Czeslaw Pospieszynski, an analyst at Bank Gdanski brokerage.
Some analysts said the expected correction was likely to be provoked by unspectacular December earnings reports released last Friday and on Monday.
Others said, however, that no clear picture had emerged from December reports as the companies' performance was distorted by end-of-year accounting operations.
Analysts saw strong support for the WIG index at 15,000-15,500 points and said the correction, likely to be followed by stabilisation later on, was likely to last until the end of the week.
They said Bank Slaski SA surged 9.9 percent in heavy turnover to its highest level since 1994, helped by a buy recommendation from the brokerage unit of Bank Handlowy SA.
Mass privatisation NFI units stayed flat in a 23-million -zloty ($7.9 million) turnover in regular trade but eased 0.3-percent in 8.8-million-zloty ($3 million) continuous trade.
Live trade turnover amounted to 9.6 million zlotys ($3.3 million) with eight stocks up, one down and nine flat.
